/*
# SimpleLayout — stack children along an axis

The stacking idiom: siblings placed one after another along
`axis`, in child order, `spacing` apart (negative overlaps). The cross axis
and all sizes stay the children's own — a child centers itself across a row
with the ordinary `y = center`. Invisible children are skipped and their
space reclaimed; a skipped child still gets the slot it would occupy, so
re-showing it needs no special case. A `Spacer` child flexes to absorb the
run's slack along the axis (between two groups it pushes them apart; one on
each side centers the run).

Written in Declare over the Layout kernel: the whole strategy is this one
pure place() — one box per laid child, aligned by index.

**Padding is the view's** (`View.padding`), and this stack obeys it without
knowing it exists: it arranges inside the room the view gives it, so a run
placed at `0` starts at the content origin, the cross-axis band `align` works
in is the room *between* the insets, and a view that sizes itself from the
stack grows by both. The inset reaches **every** child, on both axes,
`align = none` included — a child placing its own `x = 0` sits on the content
edge, not the view's, because the content box is the parent's and not this
arrangement's.

```declare
col: View [ x = 20, y = 20,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],
    View [ width = 160, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = steelblue ],
    View [ width = 120, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = cadetblue ],
    View [ width = 190, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = slategray ]
    ]
```

## axis
Which way children stack: `y` (the default) or `x`. **A bare literal, not a string** —
`axis = x`, and note that `x` here is the axis token, not the position attribute.

## spacing
The gap between adjacent children. **Negative overlaps them**, which is how a stack of
cards or avatars is built.

## align
The **cross axis** — `y` on a row, `x` on a stack. `none` (the default) leaves it to the
children, who place themselves with the ordinary `y = center`. `start | center | end`
aligns every child within the **band**: the view's own cross **content** extent — so a
column `width = 260` centres a `width = { parent.width - 32 }` child at 16, with the slack
split evenly — falling back to the **line**, the tallest (widest) laid child's extent, on a view
that derives its own cross size from these very children (reading an extent this
arrangement feeds would be a cycle, and on such a view the line *is* that extent). A
child wider than the band keeps the line, so it never hangs out both sides.
`baseline` — a row only — sits every child on one
baseline: a `Text` reports its own, and a composite **declares** which part carries it
(`baseline: number = { cap.y + cap.baseline }`); a laid child that declares none is
refused by name, at the child, and the checker says so before anything runs. A bare
literal.

## place()
The whole strategy: one box per laid child, positioned along the axis in child order.
**Every size stays the children's own, and so does the cross axis unless `align` says
otherwise** — then the boxes carry that slot too, and own it. Override it in a subclass
for custom geometry; a `Layout`'s `place()` **may** aggregate over children, which is the
one place that is allowed.
*/

class SimpleLayout extends Layout [
    axis: Axis = y,
    spacing: number = 0,
    align: CrossAlign = none,

    place() {
        const axis = this.axis
        const size = axis == "x" ? "width" : "height"
        const kids = this.laid()
        const flexing = (c) => (c).flexes === true

        // slack, only when someone flexes: the view's extent along the axis
        // minus the rigid content and the gaps between visible children.
        // A child's slot is its footprint (the scale/rotation-composed box),
        // so a scale = 0.5 child occupies half the run and a rotated card
        // reserves what it visibly covers; the box's lead compensates the
        // transform's own offset so the visible edge lands on the slot
        let each = 0
        let flexN = 0
        for (const c of kids) if (c.visible && flexing(c)) flexN = flexN + 1
        if (flexN > 0) {
            let content = 0
            let visN = 0
            for (const c of kids) {
                if (!c.visible) continue
                visN = visN + 1
                if (!flexing(c)) content = content + (c).footprint()[size]
            }
            const extent = this.contentExtent(size)
            each = Math.max(0, (extent - content - this.spacing * Math.max(0, visN - 1)) / flexN)
        }

        // the cross axis, when `align` claims it: children align within the
        // BAND — the view's own cross extent, or the largest laid cross extent
        // when the view measures these very children (viewExtent answers 0 on
        // that view: reading an extent this pass feeds is the cycle the
        // one-pass discipline forbids, and there the two agree anyway).
        // Math.max keeps an over-wide child from hanging out both sides.
        // A baseline line is the deepest declared one.
        const al = this.align
        const cross = axis == "x" ? "y" : "x"
        const crossSize = axis == "x" ? "height" : "width"
        let line = 0
        let lineBase = 0
        if (al != "none") {
            if (al == "baseline" && axis != "x") this.refuseStackBaseline()
            for (const c of kids) {
                if (!c.visible) continue
                line = Math.max(line, (c).footprint()[crossSize])
                const b = (c).baseline
                if (al == "baseline" && typeof b == "number") lineBase = Math.max(lineBase, b)
            }
            // `start` places at the band's origin and `baseline` on the shared
            // line — neither reads the band, so only center/end ask for it
            if (al == "center" || al == "end") line = Math.max(line, this.viewExtent(crossSize))
        }

        let pos = 0
        return kids.map((c) => {
            const flex = c.visible && flexing(c)
            // footprint, never bounds: the strategy must not read the slot it
            // writes (one-pass discipline). A flexing child's size is allocated
            // (box.w/h), so its footprint is never consulted — lead 0, raw slot.
            const f = flex ? null : (c).footprint()
            const lead = f == null ? 0 : (axis == "x" ? f.x : f.y)
            const box = (axis == "x" ? ({ x: pos - lead }) : ({ y: pos - lead }))
            if (flex) box[axis == "x" ? "w" : "h"] = each
            if (al != "none") {
                // start = the line's origin; center/end offset the child's
                // footprint within the line; baseline sits the child's declared
                // baseline on the line's — a child with none is refused, once,
                // and placed at start (the arrangement never breaks)
                const fc = f == null ? (c).footprint() : f
                const leadC = axis == "x" ? fc.y : fc.x
                let off = 0
                if (al == "center") off = (line - fc[crossSize]) / 2
                else if (al == "end") off = line - fc[crossSize]
                else if (al == "baseline" && axis == "x") {
                    const b = (c).baseline
                    if (typeof b == "number") off = lineBase - b
                    else if (c.visible) this.refuseBaseline(c)
                }
                box[cross] = off - (al == "baseline" ? 0 : leadC)
            }
            if (c.visible) pos = pos + (flex ? each : (f)[size]) + this.spacing
            return box
            })
        }
    ]

/*
# Icon — the drawn mark

A small monochrome mark, **drawn** rather than typed. A font's glyphs are not
marks: they are not guaranteed to be present, they rasterize differently on
every platform, and the ones that exist are the wrong shapes — a `✓` sits on the
text baseline and reads like a square-root sign, not like a checkmark. The
library's own marks — `Checkbox.mark`, `Menu.check`, the `Combobox` disclosure —
are all `Icon`s.

### Writing one

Subclass and override `draw`. Author the shape in a **16×16 box** — `unit`
converts it to whatever size the host asked for:

```declare-fragment
class SparkIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(unit, unit)
        d.strokeStyle = ink; d.lineWidth = weight / unit
        d.beginPath(); d.moveTo(8, 1); d.lineTo(8, 15); d.stroke()
        }
    ]
```

Overriding a **method** is the refinement path that works — re-opening an
inherited child is not (`cap:` on a `Button` subclass fails at instantiate), so
the shape lives in `draw` and everything adjustable is a slot.

### Size changes the drawing, not the shape

Every icon is **one path**. There are no per-size variants, no thresholds, nothing
redrawn at a breakpoint: `unit` scales the 16-box to whatever the host asked for,
so a 64px icon is the 16px icon at 4×, exactly.

The **stroke** is the deliberate exception. `d.lineWidth = weight / unit` sits
*inside* `d.scale(unit, unit)`, so the two cancel and the line lands at a constant
`weight` in **device pixels at every size**. An icon's line therefore matches the
1px rules and text weights it sits among, instead of fattening as it grows.

The cost is that the stroke-to-size ratio falls: 1.6px is 10% of a 16px icon, 5%
at 32, 2.5% at 64. Across 14–18px — chrome sizes — that is invisible. Past ~32
an icon starts reading as a fine-line drawing rather than a mark — so **this set
is built for chrome sizes**, and a large display icon (an empty-state mark, an
about-box graphic) would want the opposite: `d.lineWidth = weight` *outside* the
scale, so the line grows with the drawing. Real icon systems take a third road
and redraw per optical size range; that is a bigger undertaking than this set
needs.

### What is not an Icon

Application art. The desktop's dock icons are the case to look at before
reaching for this class: they rest at 56px and grow under the magnification
swell, they are polychrome (`gradient(hue1, hue2)` behind a hue-parameterised
drawing), and their **width animates every frame**. Each of those alone rules
them out — the constant stroke that suits a 16px mark is 2.9% of a 56px one and
reads spindly; `ink` is a single colour; and an animated width is the one thing
this set forbids.

The line is not "drawn versus not drawn" — dock art is drawn too. It is
**chrome vocabulary versus identity**. A mark that says *close*, *expand*,
*checked*, *this is the dark theme* belongs here, at a size the host states.
A mark that says *this is Calendar* does not, and belongs to the app that owns
the identity.

Desktop has both, which is what makes it the clarifying example: its menu rows
take `WindowIcon` and `CodeIcon` from this set, while its dock keeps `DockIcon`.

### Two rules

**Scale inside the body, never with the View's `scale`.** A recording rasterizes
into a canvas sized to its own ink bounds at device resolution, while `scale` is
a transform applied *after* — so `scale = { width / 16 }` would rasterize 16
pixels and stretch them. Crisp at exactly 16, soft at every other size, which is
most of them. Scaling inside the recording allocates the raster at true size
instead.

**Never animate an icon's `width`.** Reading size inside `draw` makes the
recording size-dependent: an animated size re-records **and** reallocates the
backing canvas every frame, which drops a magnifying dock of icons from 60 to
~25fps. A static size re-records once and costs nothing after: 120 icons
re-recording their *content* every frame run frame-bound at 16.6ms, cheaper
than the 120 text glyphs they replace.

Colour is not a rule — `ink` follows the provided text colour, so an icon beside
a muted label goes muted on its own, and a host that needs a different ink (a
menu row's check inverting on the hot row) simply sets it.

## ink
The mark's colour. Follows the provided `textColor`, so an icon beside a muted
label goes muted on its own. **The trap: that slot falls back to black platform-wide**,
so an icon in a context that never states a text colour renders black and vanishes on a
dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets one — `IconHost` does it for
every icon built by name.

## weight
Stroke width in **final device pixels, not authored ones**. Divide by `unit` inside
`draw` (`d.lineWidth = weight / unit`) and the scale cancels, so the line lands at a
constant weight at every size and matches the 1px rules and text it sits among.

## unit
The 16-box-to-host-size scale factor. **Multiply the path by it; divide the stroke by
it.** Every icon is one path at one size, scaled — there are no per-size variants.

## isIcon
**Internal.** The marker a layout keys on to place an icon without knowing which shape
it is — not API.

## width
Sized by the provided `iconSize`, so a menu states 16 once and every icon in it answers; a use site may set its own.

## height
Square, always — the height follows the width.

## iconSize
The mark's size, in px — a **provided value** (a host states it once, every icon beneath
answers): defaults to the nearest provided `iconSize`, overridable at the use site.

## textColor
The effective text colour the mark's `ink` follows — a **provided value**, so an icon
beside a muted label goes muted on its own; set `ink` to override.
*/

/*
# IconHost — a named icon, materialized

   A control names its icon (`iconLeft = TrashIcon`) rather than nesting one,
   because a control is a leaf and everything else about it is an attribute — and
   because an attribute is the one form where authored and bound are the same
   mechanism. `IconHost` is what turns that name into a live view, through the
   same `app.createView` seam a menu record's `icon` field uses.

   It reserves no space when empty, so a control's `contentWidth` measures only
   the slots that are actually filled and an icon-less button needs no special
   case.

   LIMITATION, deliberate for now: the name is consumed once, at construction.
   A control whose icon must CHANGE at runtime (a play/pause toggle) is not
   served by this yet — that needs a name-valued slot the runtime re-materializes
   on change, which is a runtime feature, not a library one. Every site in this
   corpus names its icon statically.

## kind
The icon **class name** to build (`"TrashIcon"`). `""` builds nothing and the host
collapses to zero width, so an icon-less control needs no special case. **Consumed once,
at construction** — assigning a new name later does not re-materialize the icon. A name
that is only ever computed needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build.

## ink
The colour handed to the icon this host builds. **`createView` cannot pass attributes,
so a PROVIDED value is the only channel that reaches it** — this provides `textColor`
for exactly that. Defaults to `theme.text` rather than the platform's inherited black,
which is what stops a host-built icon from rendering invisibly on a dark surface.

## onInit
Builds the named icon. Fires once.

## width
Zero when there is no icon to host, so an empty slot reserves nothing and an icon-less button needs no special case; else the provided `iconSize`.

## height
The icon's size whether or not one is hosted, so a row's height does not jump when an icon appears.

## visible
Present only when a kind is named.

## textColor
Passes the host's `ink` down as the provided text colour, which is what the icon's drawing reads — so a control's ink decision reaches its icon.

## iconSize
The size the built icon takes — a **provided value** (a menu row 16, a button 18);
defaults to the nearest provided `iconSize`.
*/

class IconHost extends View [
    kind: string = "",

    // Size from the context: `iconSize` defaults to the nearest provided value
    // (a host states it once — a menu row 16, a button 18 — and every icon
    // beneath answers), and a use site overrides just this one.

    iconSize: number = { this.$provided("iconSize", 16) },
    width  = { classroot.kind == "" ? 0 : this.iconSize },
    height = { this.iconSize },
    y = center,
    visible = { classroot.kind != "" },

    // The ink channel. `createView` cannot pass attributes, so the only way to
    // reach the icon it builds is a provided value — and the one `Icon.ink`
    // reads is `textColor`, which the host provides here from its `ink`.
    //
    // The default matters more than it looks: an icon that inherited a bare
    // `textColor` would fall back to black — fine on a light surface by luck,
    // invisible on a dark one. The provided theme's `text` token is a floor that
    // is never invisible in either palette.

    ink: Color = { this.$provided("theme").text },
    textColor = { classroot.ink },

    onInit() { if (this.kind != "") this.createView(this.kind, ({ })) }
    ]


class Icon extends View [
    // The marker a layout keys on, so a control can place its icon without
    // caring which shape it is.

    isIcon: boolean = true,

    // Size and ink come from the context via provided values: `iconSize` defaults
    // to the nearest provided value (a menu states 16 once and every icon answers),
    // and `textColor` to the nearest provided text colour — each overridable at the
    // use site. So `iconSize`/`textColor` on the icon win, a container's provision
    // cascades, and a bare icon has a sensible floor.

    iconSize:  number = { this.$provided("iconSize", 16) },
    textColor: Color  = { this.$provided("textColor", 0x000000) },

    width  = { this.iconSize },
    height = { this.width },
    y = center,

    // Follows the effective text colour, so an icon beside a muted label goes
    // muted on its own. State `ink` directly to override — `IconHost` does it for
    // every icon built by name.

    ink: Color = { this.textColor },
    weight: number = 1.6,        // stroke width in final pixels, not authored ones

    // 16-box → host size. Multiply the path by this; divide the stroke by it, so
    // the line keeps its true weight instead of scaling with the drawing.

    unit: number = { this.width / 16 }
    ]

/*
# Core icons

The marks the chrome uses everywhere: a chevron, a check, a close, plus/minus,
and the menu's help bulb. Each is authored in a 16×16 box and scaled to the
host's `iconSize` inside its recording (see `icon.declare`).

Geometry is a property of the **set**, not of the site: one stroke weight, round
caps and joins throughout, one path per shape, so a checkmark in a `Checkbox` and
one in a `Menu` row are the same mark. Ink stays local — a menu row inverts its
check on the hot row, a checkbox always uses `accentText`.
*/



/*
# ChevronIcon

The **disclosure** mark: a menu drops, a pane opens, a select expands. Every
disclosure in the chrome is this one class turned by its `dir`, which is what makes
them agree. For a direction that is itself the state — a sort order, a trend — reach
for `ArrowIcon` instead; the two must not look alike.

## dir
The resting orientation: `"down"` (the default), `"up"`, `"left"` or `"right"`. Sugar
over `angle`.

## angle
The rotation in radians, and **the primitive, so it can be sprung** — an `Accordion`
twisty turns in step with its pane sliding open rather than snapping between two
states. The turn lives in the recording deliberately: the mark rotates inside its
16-box while the box stays put. (The View-level `rotation` attribute turns the whole
box — the wrong tool for a glyph whose frame should not move.)

## draw()
Renders the chevron. Override to replace the mark while keeping the class's role.
*/

class ChevronIcon extends Icon [
    dir: string = "down",                       // down | up | left | right
    angle: number = { classroot.dir == "up" ? Math.PI
                    : classroot.dir == "left" ? Math.PI / 2
                    : classroot.dir == "right" ? -Math.PI / 2 : 0 },

    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.save()
        d.translate(8, 8)
        d.rotate(this.angle)
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(-3.5, -1.75)
        d.lineTo(0, 1.75)
        d.lineTo(3.5, -1.75)
        d.stroke()
        d.restore()
        }
    ]


/*
# ArrowIcon

An arrow, **not a chevron** — the two mean different things and must not look alike.
A chevron *discloses*; an arrow points at a direction that **is itself the state**:
sort ascending, a trend, a transfer. The shaft is what a chevron lacks. The two often
sit adjacent — a sort-direction control beside a sort-menu popper — and one shape for
both reads as a mistake.

## dir
Which way it points: `"up"` (the default), `"down"`, `"left"` or `"right"`.

## angle
The rotation in radians, sprungable like `ChevronIcon`'s.

## draw()
Renders the arrow.
*/

class ArrowIcon extends Icon [
    dir: string = "up",                         // up | down | left | right
    angle: number = { classroot.dir == "down" ? Math.PI
                    : classroot.dir == "left" ? -Math.PI / 2
                    : classroot.dir == "right" ? Math.PI / 2 : 0 },

    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.save()
        d.translate(8, 8)
        d.rotate(this.angle)
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(0, 5.2); d.lineTo(0, -5.2)     // the shaft is what a chevron lacks
        d.moveTo(-3.6, -1.6); d.lineTo(0, -5.2); d.lineTo(3.6, -1.6)
        d.stroke()
        d.restore()
        }
    ]


/*
# CheckIcon

The tick — a checked menu row, a `Checkbox`'s mark, a confirmation. **Ink stays
local**: a menu row inverts its check on the highlighted row while a checkbox always
uses the accent text color, so the host sets `ink` rather than the icon assuming it.

## draw()
Renders the tick. One shape, one stroke, one join — so a checkbox's mark and a menu
row's check cannot drift apart.
*/

class CheckIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.lineJoin = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3, 8.5)
        d.lineTo(6.5, 12)
        d.lineTo(13, 4.5)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# CloseIcon

The dismiss mark: a window close box, a chip's remove affordance, a dialog's corner.

## draw()
Renders the cross.
*/

class CloseIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(4.5, 4.5); d.lineTo(11.5, 11.5)
        d.moveTo(11.5, 4.5); d.lineTo(4.5, 11.5)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# PlusIcon

Add. Pairs with `MinusIcon` at the same stroke and cap, so a stepper's two ends match.

## draw()
Renders the plus.
*/

class PlusIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(8, 3.5); d.lineTo(8, 12.5)
        d.moveTo(3.5, 8); d.lineTo(12.5, 8)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# MinusIcon

Remove, and the partially-checked state of a tri-state box. Pairs with `PlusIcon`.

## draw()
Renders the bar.
*/

class MinusIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.strokeStyle = this.ink
        d.lineWidth = this.weight / this.unit
        d.lineCap = "round"
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3.5, 8); d.lineTo(12.5, 8)
        d.stroke()
        }
    ]


/*
# LightbulbIcon

The help affordance — the one FILLED mark in a stroked set: a continuous
teardrop of glass over a three-bar tapering base.

## draw()
Renders the bulb. **This one mark is filled, and does not answer to `weight`**
— the contour carries its weight in the outline itself, so there is no stroke
to widen. The bulb keeps its own visual weight at every rung.
*/

// The one filled mark: the contour is the drawing — glass as a continuous
// teardrop, the base as three tapering bars — so `weight` has no stroke to
// act on here. No y-flip anywhere: the path counts down, like this canvas.

class LightbulbIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(this.unit, this.unit)
        d.fillStyle = this.ink
        d.beginPath()
        d.moveTo(3.4, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(3.4, 6.876, 4.982, 7.529, 5.422, 12.115)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.449, 12.363, 5.587, 12.521, 5.848, 12.521)
        d.lineTo(10.152, 12.521)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.42, 12.521, 10.558, 12.363, 10.585, 12.115)
        d.bezierCurveTo(11.025, 7.529, 12.6, 6.876, 12.6, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(12.6, 1.863, 10.572, 0.0, 8.0, 0.0)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.428, 0.0, 3.4, 1.863, 3.4, 4.235)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(4.438, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(4.438, 2.379, 6.068, 1.038, 8.0, 1.038)
        d.bezierCurveTo(9.932, 1.038, 11.562, 2.379, 11.562, 4.235)
        d.bezierCurveTo(11.562, 6.209, 10.255, 6.676, 9.636, 11.483)
        d.lineTo(6.37, 11.483)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.745, 6.676, 4.438, 6.209, 4.438, 4.235)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(5.827, 14.006)
        d.lineTo(10.18, 14.006)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.407, 14.006, 10.578, 13.827, 10.578, 13.6)
        d.bezierCurveTo(10.578, 13.38, 10.407, 13.202, 10.18, 13.202)
        d.lineTo(5.827, 13.202)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.6, 13.202, 5.422, 13.38, 5.422, 13.6)
        d.bezierCurveTo(5.422, 13.827, 5.6, 14.006, 5.827, 14.006)
        d.closePath()
        d.moveTo(8.0, 16.0)
        d.bezierCurveTo(9.066, 16.0, 9.953, 15.477, 10.021, 14.687)
        d.lineTo(5.985, 14.687)
        d.bezierCurveTo(6.034, 15.477, 6.927, 16.0, 8.0, 16.0)
        d.closePath()
        d.fill()
        }
    ]

/*
# TextLabel

A `Text` that centers its ink in its parent's height — the vertical placement a
*label* wants, as opposed to a paragraph. Use it for the text inside a control
or any centered caption; use plain `Text` for flowing copy.

Why it exists. `y = center` on a plain `Text` centers the geometric box (the
ordinary meaning, matching every other view). But a label sitting in a box wants
its **letterforms** optically centered, not the font's box with its asymmetric
ascent/descent leading — otherwise the text reads a hair low. `TextLabel`
supplies a `y` that centers the cap band (cap-top to baseline), the optical
centre for a label:

    y = { parent.height / 2 - this.baseline + this.capHeight / 2 }

That expression cap-centres the label: the ink sits centred by its cap band rather
than by its box, which is what reads as centred for a label. It is written out here,
once, instead of at every use site. It is a plain constraint over the Text's own live
metric facts
(`baseline`, `capHeight`, measured from the effective font), so it re-centers
when the font, the size, or the parent's height changes. Override `y` on an
instance to opt out.

The centre is the cap band because that is what the platform control themes
(Cupertino, Mountain View, Redmond) are matched against.

## y
Centres the ink on the parent's height by its cap band — baseline and cap height — rather than by the line box, which is what a label beside a control wants and a paragraph does not.
*/

class TextLabel extends Text [
    y = { parent.height / 2 - this.baseline + this.capHeight / 2 }
    ]

/*
# 50 Birds — a field guide with a quiz, and the teaching app for `location` + `waypoint`

Every value in this program lives in exactly one of three homes, sorted by the
stranger test (guide ch. 13 — *would you hand it to a stranger?*):

  location  the addresses — "" (the shelf), "b/<slug>" (one bird's page,
            crawlable and shareable), "quiz" (the quiz room). The URL shows
            these and nothing else.
  waypoint  the step — one string, "<seeds>|<answers>|<shown>", from which
            the entire quiz round derives: which ten birds, what you answered,
            which card is up, even the decoy choices (deterministic — no stored
            shuffle). Every pick and every Next writes it, so each is a history
            entry: the Back button retraces the quiz action by action, the URL
            sitting motionless at #quiz the whole time. A coordinate rides on
            its entry, so it comes back by traversal only: reload the page (or
            open a shared #quiz link) and you get the invitation and a fresh
            round, because the URL is all an arrival has to rebuild from — one
            Back, though, and the old round is still on the entry behind you.
  ordinary  everything else — hovers, the loaded flag, and the flights (the
            plate's zoom from shelf tile to page, and its return home).
            The flights are the third row made vivid: nobody
            shares a zoom, so their rects are plain attributes and history
            never hears of them. Arrivals animate only from gestures — a
            pasted URL simply is its page — but the journey home plays for
            the Back button too, armed inside `onFollow`: the hook is the one
            door a link click and a traversal both pass through, which is
            exactly what lets a motion answer Back without any handler running.

Around those three: every tile and cross-reference is a `link` (a real <a> —
hover preview, ⌘-click, the crawler's edge), so the crawl walks the shelf to
all fifty pages with no route table and no server; `onFollow` is the
renamed-pages door — Audubon's own names ("carolina-parrot",
"great-footed-hawk") redirect to today's slugs, so a 150-year-old citation
still lands; and `appName` derives per place, so the history menu lists real
titles. The plates are Audubon's, public domain; the data is a build-time
fixture (birds.json beside this file), which is what makes the whole guide
crawlable from a static host.
*/

// the palette: paper #F7F3E8 · mat #FFFDF6 · ink #2B2825 · muted #8A8272 ·
// hair #E2DACA · accent (oxblood) #7A3B2E · right #4A6B4D · wrong #9A4632

// ── one plate in a frame: cream mat, hairline, the engraving contained ───────

class Plate extends View [ fill = #FFFDF6, stroke = stroke(1, #E2DACA), clip = true,
    slug: string = "",
    lift: number = 0,                            // 0 = at rest, 1 = raised (hover) — the shadow deepens
    shadow = { shadow(0, 2 + 5 * this.lift, 9 + 13 * this.lift, colorWithAlpha(0x000000, 0x24)) },

    // the cream mat is the frame's own inset — the engraving simply fills the
    // room it is given, and the hairline still runs around the outside

    padding = 8,
    pic: Image [ width = 100%, height = 100%,
        stretches = contain, source = { classroot.slug == "" ? "" : "plates/" + classroot.slug + ".jpg" } ]
    ]


// ── a shelf tile: plate + caption, the whole thing one link to the bird ──────

class Tile extends View [ width = { this.root.tileW }, height = { this.root.tileW + 44 },
    link = { "#b/" + this.$data(["slug"]) },
    x = { (this.$data(["gi"]) % this.root.cols) * (this.root.tileW + 18) },
    y = { (Math.floor(this.$data(["gi"]) / this.root.cols)) * (this.root.tileW + 62) },
    hoverT: number = 0,
    Spring [ attribute = hoverT, to = { classroot.hovered ? 1 : 0 }, stiffness = 220, damping = 20, epsilon = 0.001 ],

    // the click captures this plate's place on the shelf before the link
    // navigates (onClick beside a link runs first) — the flight's origin

    onClick() { this.root.beginFlight(this.frame) },

    // while this bird is flying home its plate is simply not here — bare paper
    // and a caption waiting for it (app.inFlight). The flyer wears the same mat
    // and lands on this exact rect, so the swap at touchdown is invisible.

    frame: Plate [ width = 100%, height = { parent.width }, slug = { this.$data(["slug"]) },
        visible = { !this.root.inFlight("" + this.$data(["slug"])) },
        lift = { classroot.hoverT },
        scale = { 1 + 0.03 * classroot.hoverT }, pivotX = { this.width / 2 }, pivotY = { this.height / 2 } ],
    cap: Text [ y = { parent.width + 8 }, width = 100%, textAlign = center, wrap = false,
        fontSize = 13, textColor = { classroot.hovered ? 0x7A3B2E : 0x2B2825 }, text = { this.$data(["name"]) } ],
    lost: Text [ y = { parent.width + 26 }, width = 100%, textAlign = center, wrap = false,
        fontSize = 11, textColor = #9A4632, visible = { this.$data(["status"]) == "extinct" }, text = "extinct" ]
    ]


// ── one answer choice in the quiz ────────────────────────────────────────────

class Choice extends View [ width = 100%, height = 44, cornerRadius = 8,
    pick: number = -1,                           // the bird index this button answers with
    label: string = "",
    state: string = "",                          // "" | "right" | "wrong" | "missed"
    fill = { this.state == "right" ? 0xDCE8DC : this.state == "wrong" ? 0xEFDCD6 : this.hovered ? 0xF2EDE0 : 0xFFFDF6 },
    stroke = { stroke(1, this.state == "right" ? 0x4A6B4D : this.state == "wrong" ? 0x9A4632 : 0xE2DACA) },
    onClick() { this.root.pick(this.pick) },
    t: TextLabel [ x = 16, fontSize = 15,
        textColor = { parent.state == "wrong" ? 0x9A4632 : 0x2B2825 }, text = { classroot.label } ]
    ]


// ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

App [ width = { this.root.hostWidth > 0 ? this.root.hostWidth : 1200 }, fill = #F7F3E8, textColor = #2B2825,

    // One face for the whole book, declared once and provided: every Text below
    // reads it, so no run names a family and changing the book's typeface is a
    // one-line edit.

    serif: Font [ family = "Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif" ],
    fontFamily = { this.root.serif },

    location = "",
    waypoint = "",
    appName = { this.root.bird != null ? "" + this.root.bird.name + " · 50 Birds" : this.root.dest == "quiz" ? "The Quiz · 50 Birds" : "50 Birds" },

    /* Environment-aware, the calendar's idiom: standalone the fixture sits
       beside the app; hosted, the embedder passes env.base (its own
       transport's path to this app's home) and the same relative address
       resolves through it — `auto` refetches when base lands after init. */

    data: DataSource [ auto = true, url = { this.$hostProvided("base", "") + "birds.json" } ],
    birds: array = { this.data.loaded ? this.data.value.groups.flatMap((g) => g.birds) : [] },

    // ── location → the address, parsed (grammar: "" · "b/<slug>" · "quiz") ──

    dest:    string = { this.root.location.split("/")[0] },
    slug:    string = { this.root.location.slice(0, 2) == "b/" ? this.root.location.slice(2) : "" },
    bird:    object = { this.root.slug == "" ? null : (this.root.birds.find((b) => b.slug == this.root.slug) ?? null) },
    atShelf: boolean = { this.root.dest != "quiz" && this.root.bird == null },

    // Audubon's own names still resolve — the renamed-pages door (onFollow).
    // A 150-year-old citation lands on today's slug; everything else passes.

    onFollow(ref: string) -> string {
        const old = ({ "carolina-parrot": "carolina-parakeet", "great-footed-hawk": "peregrine-falcon",
            "mocking-bird": "northern-mockingbird", "white-headed-eagle": "bald-eagle" })
        const renamed = ref.slice(0, 3) == "#b/" ? old[ref.slice(3)] : undefined
        // The return flight is armed here, in the hook, and not in any click
        // handler — because the hook is the one door every arrival passes
        // through, the Back button included, and Back runs no handler. One
        // condition covers both ways home: the "← the whole shelf" link and a
        // history traversal each announce themselves as an arrival at "#",
        // and if we are leaving a bird when that arrives, its plate flies
        // back to its tile (the inverse of beginFlight, derived from data
        // rather than a captured rect, so it lands on the right tile even if
        // prev/next walked us far from the bird we originally opened).
        if (ref == "#" && this.root.bird != null) this.root.armReturn()
        return renamed != undefined ? "#b/" + renamed : ref
        },

    // ── waypoint → the session, parsed ("<seeds>|<answers>|<shown>") ─────────
    // The whole round is a pure function of this one string: ten bird indices
    // drawn at start, the answers so far, and which card is up. The decoys
    // derive too — fixed co-prime offsets from the right answer, ordered by a
    // rotation the answer picks — so a restored waypoint rebuilds the exact
    // card, choices and all. Nothing about the round is stored anywhere else.

    seeds:    number[] = { this.root.waypoint.split("|")[0] == "" ? [] : this.root.waypoint.split("|")[0].split(",").map(Number) },
    answers:  number[] = { (this.root.waypoint.split("|")[1] ?? "") == "" ? [] : this.root.waypoint.split("|")[1].split(",").map(Number) },
    shown:    number   = { Number(this.root.waypoint.split("|")[2] ?? 0) },
    started:  boolean  = { this.root.seeds.length > 0 },
    finished: boolean  = { this.root.started && this.root.shown >= this.root.seeds.length },
    answer:   number   = { this.root.started && !this.root.finished ? this.root.seeds[this.root.shown] : -1 },
    picked:   number   = { this.root.answers.length > this.root.shown ? this.root.answers[this.root.shown] : -1 },
    revealed: boolean  = { this.root.picked >= 0 },
    score:    number   = { this.root.answers.filter((a, t) => a == this.root.seeds[t]).length },
    choices:  number[] = { this.root.answer < 0 ? [] : this.root.rotate([this.root.answer, (this.root.answer + 13) % 50, (this.root.answer + 27) % 50, (this.root.answer + 41) % 50], this.root.answer % 4) },
    rotate(a: number[], n: number) -> number[] { return a.slice(n).concat(a.slice(0, n)) },

    // the session's verbs — each one write, each one history entry

    startQuiz() {
        const drawn = []
        while (drawn.length < 10) {
            const n = Math.floor(Math.random() * 50)
            if (drawn.indexOf(n) < 0) drawn.push(n)
        }
        this.root.waypoint = drawn.join(",") + "||0"
        },
    pick(n: number) {
        if (this.root.revealed || this.root.answer < 0) return
        this.root.waypoint = this.root.seeds.join(",") + "|" + this.root.answers.concat([n]).join(",") + "|" + this.root.shown
        },
    advance() {
        if (!this.root.revealed) return
        this.root.waypoint = this.root.seeds.join(",") + "|" + this.root.answers.join(",") + "|" + (this.root.shown + 1)
        },

    nameOf(n: number) -> string { return this.root.birds.length > n && n >= 0 ? "" + this.root.birds[n].name : "" },
    slugOf(n: number) -> string { return this.root.birds.length > n && n >= 0 ? "" + this.root.birds[n].slug : "" },

    // ── the flight — one plate traveling from its shelf tile to the page ─────
    // The same object leaves its grid slot and lands as the page's plate, so
    // the transition reads as continuity, not replacement. Note what the
    // flight is not: it is neither an address nor a step. A pasted `#b/…` URL
    // and a Back press both land with no entrance — a URL should simply be
    // the page, and Back restores where you were rather than re-performing
    // the click that took you there. So the captured rect lives in ordinary
    // attributes (flyW < 0 = none), and only a real click ever starts the
    // animator.

    flyX: number = -1,                           // the tile plate's rect, in content coordinates
    flyY: number = -1,
    flyW: number = -1,
    lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number) -> number { return a + (b - a) * t },
    beginFlight(v: View) {
        const o = v.rootOrigin()                 // content coordinates, scroll-aware
        this.root.flyX = o.x
        this.root.flyY = o.y
        this.root.flyW = v.width
        this.root.page.fly.start()
        },
    turnPage() {
        // a within-page turn (prev/next, a cross-reference): no shelf rect to
        // fly from, so the entrance is a plain dissolve on the same animator
        this.root.flyW = -1
        this.root.page.fly.start()
        },
    armReturn() {
        // the inverse journey (see onFollow): remember who is going home, and
        // fly. The flyer below derives both endpoints — the page's resting
        // plate and the bird's own tile — so nothing else needs capturing.
        this.root.retSlug = "" + this.root.bird.slug
        this.root.ret.start()
        },
    retSlug: string = "",
    retT:    number = 1,
    ret:     Animator [ attribute = retT, from = 0, to = 1, duration = 340, motion = cubicOut ],

    // One plate, one place. While a bird is flying home its shelf slot is bare
    // paper — the plate is not in two places, it is in the air — so the eye
    // follows a single object into the gap it left. The tile asks this of every
    // plate it draws; at rest it is always false.

    inFlight(slug: string) -> boolean { return this.root.retT < 1 && this.root.retSlug == slug },
    tileRectOf(slug: string) -> object {
        // a tile's resting rect on the shelf, re-derived from the same
        // arithmetic the shelf lays out with — content coordinates, so the
        // flyer lands true at any scroll position
        const b = this.root.birds.find((x) => x.slug == slug)
        if (b == null || !this.root.data.loaded) return ({ x: 0, y: 0, w: 0 })
        let y = 84
        for (const g of this.root.data.value.groups) {
            if (g.name == b.group) break
            y += 34 + Math.ceil(Number(g.count) / this.root.cols) * (this.root.tileW + 62) + 34
        }
        y += 34 + Math.floor(Number(b.gi) / this.root.cols) * (this.root.tileW + 62)
        return ({ x: this.root.colX + (Number(b.gi) % this.root.cols) * (this.root.tileW + 18), y: y, w: this.root.tileW })
        },

    // ── responsive column ────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    colW:  number = { Math.min(1060, this.root.width - 48) },
    colX:  number = { (this.root.width - this.root.colW) / 2 },
    cols:  number = { this.root.colW < 560 ? 2 : this.root.colW < 840 ? 3 : 5 },
    tileW: number = { (this.root.colW - (this.root.cols - 1) * 18) / this.root.cols },

    // ── fixed chrome: the masthead rides the window over the page scroll ─────

    bar: View [ ignoreScroll = true, x = 0, y = 0, width = { this.root.width }, height = 58, fill = #F7F3E8F2,
        stroke = [null, null, stroke(1, #E2DACA), null],   // the rule under the masthead, not a child view
        mark: Text [ x = { this.root.colX }, y = center, fontSize = 19, letterSpacing = 2,
            text = "50 BIRDS", link = "#", textColor = #2B2825 ],
        sub: Text [ x = { this.root.colX + 118 }, y = 22, fontSize = 12, textColor = #8A8272, wrap = false,
            visible = { this.root.colW >= 700 }, text = "the plates of John James Audubon, 1827–1838" ],
        quizLink: Text [ x = { this.root.colX + this.root.colW - 64 }, y = center, fontSize = 14,
            link = "#quiz", text = "The Quiz", textColor = { this.root.dest == "quiz" ? 0x7A3B2E : 0x2B2825 } ]
        ],

    // ═══ the shelf — every plate, grouped; each tile a link (an address) ═════

    shelf: View [ x = { this.root.colX }, y = 84, width = { this.root.colW }, visible = { this.root.atShelf },
        datapath = { this.root.data.loaded ? this.root.data.value : null },
        layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 34 ],
        loadNote: Text [ fontSize = 14, textColor = #8A8272, visible = { !this.root.data.loaded },
            text = { this.root.data.failed ? "The field guide failed to load: " + this.root.data.error : "Fetching the plates…" } ],
        Section [ datapath = :groups[], key = :name ],
        credit: Text [ width = 100%, fontSize = 12, textColor = #8A8272, lineHeight = 1.5,
            text = "Plates: John James Audubon, The Birds of America (1827–1838), public domain — high-resolution scans courtesy of the National Audubon Society. Prose written for this field guide." ],
        pad: View [ width = 1, height = 56 ]
        ],

    // ═══ one bird — a page with an address you could hand to anyone ══════════

    page: View [ x = { this.root.colX }, y = 84, width = { this.root.colW }, visible = { this.root.bird != null },
        datapath = { this.root.bird },

        // the arrival scalar: 0 = just left the shelf, 1 = at rest. A clicked
        // tile flies the plate here (geometry below); a page turn dissolves;
        // a deep link or a traversal never starts it, so flyT rests at 1 and
        // the page is simply present — the entrance belongs to the gesture
        // that caused it, never to the URL or the Back button.

        flyT: number = 1,
        fly: Animator [ attribute = flyT, from = 0, to = 1, duration = 340, motion = cubicOut ],
        wide: boolean = { this.root.colW >= 760 },
        plateW: number = { this.wide ? Math.min(560, this.root.colW - 380) : this.root.colW },

        // the traveling object: from the captured tile rect (in page-local
        // terms) to the resting frame — or already at rest when no flight

        frame: Plate [
            x = { this.root.flyW < 0 ? 0 : this.root.lerp(this.root.flyX - this.root.colX, 0, parent.flyT) },
            y = { this.root.flyW < 0 ? 0 : this.root.lerp(this.root.flyY - 84, 0, parent.flyT) },
            width = { this.root.flyW < 0 ? parent.plateW : this.root.lerp(this.root.flyW, parent.plateW, parent.flyT) },
            height = { this.width * 1.05 },
            opacity = { this.root.flyW < 0 ? parent.flyT : 1 },
            slug = { "" + (this.$data(["slug"]) ?? "") } ],
        info: View [ x = { parent.wide ? parent.plateW + 36 : 0 }, y = { parent.wide ? 8 : parent.plateW * 1.05 + 24 },
            width = { parent.wide ? parent.width - parent.plateW - 36 : parent.width },
            opacity = { parent.flyT },               // the details fade up as the plate lands
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 14 ],
            name: Text [ fontSize = 30, width = 100%, text = { "" + (this.$data(["name"]) ?? "") } ],
            latin: Text [ fontSize = 15, textColor = #8A8272, italic = true, text = { "" + (this.$data(["latin"]) ?? "") } ],
            plateNo: Text [ fontSize = 13, textColor = #8A8272,
                text = { this.$data(["plate"]) == null ? "" : "Plate " + this.$data(["plate"]) + (this.$data(["audubonName"]) != this.$data(["name"]) ? "  ·  Audubon called it the " + this.$data(["audubonName"]) : "") } ],
            gone: Text [ fontSize = 13, textColor = #9A4632, visible = { this.$data(["status"]) == "extinct" }, text = "EXTINCT" ],
            prose: Text [ width = 100%, fontSize = 16, lineHeight = 1.55, text = { "" + (this.$data(["prose"]) ?? "") } ],
            kinHead: Text [ fontSize = 13, textColor = #8A8272, text = "SEE ALSO" ],
            kinRow: View [ width = 100%, height = 24,
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 18 ],
                k1: Text [ fontSize = 14, textColor = #7A3B2E, wrap = false,
                    onClick() { this.root.turnPage() },
                    link = { "#b/" + this.$data(["kin",{"i":0}]) }, text = { this.root.birds.length > 0 ? "" + (this.root.birds.find((b) => b.slug == this.$data(["kin",{"i":0}]))?.name ?? "") : "" }
                    ],
                k2: Text [ fontSize = 14, textColor = #7A3B2E, wrap = false,
                    onClick() { this.root.turnPage() },
                    link = { "#b/" + this.$data(["kin",{"i":1}]) }, text = { this.root.birds.length > 0 ? "" + (this.root.birds.find((b) => b.slug == this.$data(["kin",{"i":1}]))?.name ?? "") : "" }
                    ]
                ],
            walk: View [ width = 100%, height = 30,
                prev: Text [ x = 0, y = center, fontSize = 14, textColor = #8A8272, wrap = false,
                    onClick() { this.root.turnPage() },
                    visible = { this.$data(["i"]) > 0 }, link = { "#b/" + this.root.slugOf(this.$data(["i"]) - 1) }, text = { "← " + this.root.nameOf(this.$data(["i"]) - 1) }
                    ],
                next: Text [ x = end, y = center, fontSize = 14, textColor = #8A8272, wrap = false,
                    onClick() { this.root.turnPage() },
                    visible = { this.$data(["i"]) < 49 }, link = { "#b/" + this.root.slugOf(this.$data(["i"]) + 1) }, text = { this.root.nameOf(this.$data(["i"]) + 1) + " →" }
                    ]
                ],
            home: Text [ fontSize = 14, textColor = #8A8272, link = "#", text = "← the whole shelf" ],
            pad: View [ width = 1, height = 56 ]
            ],
        platePad: View [ x = 0, y = { parent.plateW * 1.05 }, width = 1, height = 72 ],

        // close the page: the same address as the masthead and "the whole
        // shelf" (`#` — the shelf), as a box where a reader expects one. It
        // fades up with the details, and Back still works: closing is a
        // follow, so it makes an entry like any other move.

        closeBox: View [ x = { parent.width - 34 }, y = 6, width = 28, height = 28, cornerRadius = 14,
            fill = #F7F3E8F2, stroke = stroke(1, #E2DACA), link = "#", opacity = { parent.flyT },
            mark: CloseIcon [ x = center, y = center, iconSize = 15, ink = #8A8272 ]
            ]
        ],

    // ═══ the quiz — one address, a whole session of history entries ══════════

    quiz: View [ visible = { this.root.destinationOf(this.root.location) == "quiz" }, shows = "quiz", x = { this.root.colX }, y = 84, width = { Math.min(620, this.root.colW) },
        card: View [ width = 100%,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 16 ],

            // before a round: the invitation (also where a shared #quiz link
            // lands — the URL carried the place, deliberately not the session)

            invite: View [ width = 100%, visible = { !this.root.started },
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 14 ],
                h: Text [ fontSize = 26, text = "Name the bird." ],
                p: Text [ width = 100%, fontSize = 15, lineHeight = 1.5, textColor = #8A8272,
                    text = "Ten plates, four names each. The Back button un-asks a question — try it mid-round and watch the URL not care." ],
                go: View [ width = 180, height = 44, cornerRadius = 8, fill = #7A3B2E,
                    onClick() { this.root.startQuiz() },
                    t: Text [ y = center, width = 100%, textAlign = center,
                        fontSize = 16, textColor = #F7F3E8, text = "Begin" ]
                    ]
                ],

            // the live card — everything on it derives from app.waypoint

            live: View [ width = 100%, visible = { this.root.started && !this.root.finished },
                shownT: number = 0,
                Spring [ attribute = shownT, to = { this.root.shown }, stiffness = 190, damping = 24, epsilon = 0.002 ],
                x = { (this.root.shown - this.shownT) * -42 },
                opacity = { 1 - Math.min(1, Math.abs(this.root.shown - this.shownT)) * 0.55 },
                layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 14 ],
                tally: Text [ fontSize = 13, textColor = #8A8272,
                    text = { "Question " + (this.root.shown + 1) + " of " + this.root.seeds.length + "   ·   " + this.root.score + " right so far" } ],

class Section extends View [ width = 100%,
